title: Technical-risk handoff and 15m operational checklist (facilitator script + escape hatches)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact facilitator script + prep checklist for a 15-minute technical-risk handoff that runs inside or adjacent to a QBR. Target audience: CS lead (facilitator), Solutions Engineer (SE) / Technical Owner, and the customer technical stakeholder. Goal: surface current technical risks, agree immediate mitigations or 'escape hatches', and create a 48-hour action with owners so renewal/production risk is managed.
agenda:
1) 0:00–1:00 — Quick context (CS lead): objective of this micro-session and desired outcome (1 sentence).
2) 1:00–5:00 — SE highlights top 3 signals (latency, error rate, regressions) with concrete evidence and severity.
3) 5:00–9:00 — Customer technical stakeholder reads back impact and adds any missing items (priority ordering).
4) 9:00–12:00 — Facilitated mitigation options: immediate workaround, fallback plan, escalation path.
5) 12:00–14:00 — Decision and owner assignment (who will do what in 48h).
6) 14:00–15:00 — Quick close: confirm follow-up touchpoint, communication channel, and success metric to judge resolved.
facilitation_script:
Intro (CS lead, 30s): 
  ‘We have a focused 15-minute handoff to ensure any active technical risks are captured and owned. We’ll surface the top signal, confirm impact, pick a short mitigation, and assign a 48-hour owner.’

SE highlight (SE, up to 4m):
  - Open with the observable: metric, time window, and how we detected it (ex: 90th p95 latency rose from 120ms -> 460ms for /generate from 03/01 08:40–09:10).
  - Evidence: link to dashboard or logs, sample request ID(s), error messages if relevant.
  - Scope: % of requests/users affected and whether it’s reproducible.
  - Initial guess/root-cause hypothesis and immediate risk (regression, capacity, model change).

Customer readback (Customer tech, up to 4m):
  - Confirm impact on their workflows or SLAs, and immediate user visible effects.
  - Call out any internal downstream processes that amplify the impact (batch jobs, analytics backfills).

Mitigation options (Facilitator + SE, up to 3m):
  - Option A (fastest): revert-to-last-stable-config or pin to previous model variant (when applicable). Pros/cons and estimated time to implement.
  - Option B (workaround): routing subset of traffic to Dedicated/backup region or enable kv-prefix caching for hot prompts.
  - Option C (monitor only): add stricter alerting threshold + temporary rate-limit until patch.

Decision + owner (Facilitator, 2m):
  - Ask: ‘Which mitigation do we execute now?’ Record decision in the decision ledger and assign 48h owner + one backup. Set a hard follow-up checkpoint (time + channel).

Close (Facilitator, 30s):
  - Restate the owner, the acceptance criteria for closure, and the follow-up meeting (15m update or Slack confirmation by X time).

Suggested language for sensitive situations:
  - If customer calls out production user impact: ‘We hear you — priority is minimizing user impact. We will execute the fastest safe mitigation and confirm within 2 hours.’
  - If root cause not known: ‘We will triage with triage label CS-PRIORITY and run the rollback path in parallel if impact increases.’
prep_checklist:
Before the micro-session (CS lead + SE):
  - Verify dashboards: include p95/p99, error rate, throughput for the last 24h and last 7d. Paste links in the meeting note.
  - Grab 2–3 representative request IDs and one stack trace or error payload.
  - Validate who has permission to change routing or redeploy models (names + quick contacts).
  - Pre-stage rollback/variant pin commands or recipes in a private doc (copy commands so SE can run them without typing).
  - Pre-create a JIRA/issue with CS-PRIORITY label and add stakeholders so we have an audit trail.
  - Add the follow-up 15m slot to the calendar (default: 24–48h after handoff).
escape_hatches_and_playbook_snippets:
Common surprises + immediate escape hatches:
  - Symptom: sudden p95 spike after a model version rollout.
    Escape hatch: immediate pin to previous model variant using model-pin API (SE script available). If pin fails, shift 25% traffic to backup region and enable caching for repeated prompts.

  - Symptom: intermittent tokenization / request parsing errors for a customer-specific prompt.
    Escape hatch: add a pre-filtering Lambda to sanitize prompt inputs for 48 hours and remove problematic characters; open a bug with model-onboarding team for 7-day fix.

  - Symptom: missing logs / telemetry for a subset of requests (can't reproduce).
    Escape hatch: enable request-level debug tracing for the affected customer ID for 2 hours, capture one failing session, then disable (to limit cost).

  - Symptom: surge in cost due to runaway batch job hitting embeddings.
    Escape hatch: set an emergency rate-limit on embeddings route for the customer and schedule a follow-up deep-dive with their data team.

  - Symptom: latency increases when KV cache invalidation occurs after deployment.
    Escape hatch: temporarily disable aggressive cache TTL invalidation and restart warmers; if not feasible, accept short-term compute bump and isolate tenant to dedicated capacity if on Dedicated plan.

Operational run commands (copyable lines for SE):
  - Pin model: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/{proj}/models/pin" -d '{"model":"gptx-1.1","variant":"v1"}' (SE must replace placeholders).
  - Create incident issue: jira create --project CS --type Incident --summary "Customer X: latency spike" --labels CS-PRIORITY
  - Enable debug tracing: opsctl tracing enable --tenant {tenant} --duration 120m
decision_ledger_template:
Decision ledger (one row per handoff):
  - Decision ID: (CS-YYYYMMDD-N)
  - Symptom summary: short sentence
  - Chosen mitigation: Option A/B/C
  - Owner: Name (primary)
  - Backup owner: Name (backup)
  - Due by: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (timezone)
  - Acceptance criteria: how we will judge resolved (metric + timeframe)
  - Follow-up slot: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM + channel
  - Linked artifacts: Jira ID / Confluence / dashboard link
post_meeting_template_and_followups:
Within 30 minutes after close (CS lead):
  - Update the JIRA issue with the decision ledger row and tag stakeholders.
  - Post a concise summary to customer and internal #cs-technical-handoffs channel: symptom, decision, owner, due time.
  - If mitigation is rollback/pin, confirm once completed and capture before/after p95/p99 stats.
  - If no immediate mitigation chosen, require an interim monitoring plan and threshold for auto-escalation.

48-hour closure criteria checklist:
  - Owner executed mitigation OR substantial progress on permanent fix.
  - Acceptance metric met (p95 restored or error rate reduced to agreed baseline).
  - Customer confirmation of reduced impact (email or Slack).
  - JIRA updated with final notes and next steps for longer-term work.
notes_and_tips:
- Keep the micro-session laser-focused; the goal is a working 48-hour plan, not a root-cause deep dive.
- Use this micro-session to surface any blockers that require cross-org support (SRE/infra/product). If blockers exist, elevate to the 90-minute deep-technical QBR lane.
- For enterprise customers with SLAs, ensure legal/commercial stakeholders are looped if mitigation changes billing or capacity commitments.
- If the customer uses Private deployment, confirm who has access to their VPC controls before recommending regional failover.
- Add standard tags to Jira: CS-PRIORITY, severity-2, customer-{id}.

Example short script to paste into meeting notes (one paragraph):
  ‘We ran a focused 15-minute technical handoff to capture the latency spike on /generate. SE observed p95 rise to 460ms for ~12% of requests between 08:40–09:10. Customer confirmed user-visible latency on inference flows. Action: pin to model v1.3 (SE: Marco Ruiz, due 2026-02-21 11:00 PST). Follow-up check in 4 hours; closure criteria: p95 < 180ms for 95% of traffic and customer confirmation.’

Open questions / follow-ups for playbook owners:
  - Should we add an automated ‘hand-off-ready’ checklist to calendar invites? (Pros: faster prep. Cons: extra noise.)
  - Do we need a dedicated short-call SRE rota for QBR timeblocks?
  - Verify whether private-deploy customers need different escape hatch recipes (doc to author: SE-runbook-private-deployments).

Revision history: draft v0.1 — initial consolidated notes from CS/SE sync (Priya Iyer, 2025-11-12). v0.2 — added operational commands and escape hatches (Marco Ruiz, 2025-12-09). v0.3 — tightened facilitator script and added decision ledger template (Samira Patel, 2026-02-20).
